cards.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
cards.blurb: The undisputed king of red wines, producing full-bodied wines with blackcurrant, cedar, and spice notes.

cards.name: Pinot Noir
cards.blurb: Known as the heartbreak grape for its difficulty to grow, it produces elegant wines with cherry and earthy notes.

cards.name: Chardonnay
cards.blurb: The world's most versatile white grape, acting as a canvas for winemakers to craft everything from crisp to buttery styles.

cards.name: Merlot
cards.blurb: A soft and velvety red grape that produces approachable wines with plum and chocolate flavors.

cards.name: Syrah
cards.blurb: A powerful grape producing intense wines with pepper, smoke, and dark fruit characteristics.

cards.name: Sauvignon Blanc
cards.blurb: A zesty and herbaceous white grape known for its crisp acidity and distinctive citrus and green notes.

cards.name: Riesling
cards.blurb: An aromatic white grape with exceptional purity and high acidity that ages remarkably well.

cards.name: Nebbiolo
cards.blurb: A legendary Italian grape producing pale-colored wines with massive tannins and floral aromas of tar and roses.

cards.name: Sangiovese
cards.blurb: Italy's most planted red grape, producing savory wines with vibrant cherry and tomato leaf characters.

cards.name: Grenache
cards.blurb: A sweet red fruit-driven grape that produces wines high in alcohol with strawberry and raspberry flavors.

cards.name: Tempranillo
cards.blurb: Spain's noble grape variety, producing elegant wines with leather, tobacco, and red berry notes.

cards.name: Malbec
cards.blurb: Originally from Cahors, France, this dark and inky grape has become Argentina's signature variety.

cards.name: Cabernet Franc
cards.blurb: The parent grape of Cabernet Sauvignon, known for its herbaceous character with bell pepper and raspberry notes.

cards.name: Chenin Blanc
cards.blurb: An incredibly versatile chameleon grape capable of producing dry, sweet, and sparkling wines.

cards.name: Viognier
cards.blurb: A perfumed and aromatic white grape producing full-bodied wines with peach, tangerine, and honeysuckle notes.

cards.name: Gamay
cards.blurb: A fruity and fresh grape that produces light, gulpable wines perfect for serving slightly chilled.

cards.name: Zinfandel
cards.blurb: A bold and jammy grape that produces high-alcohol wines with ripe berry and spice characteristics.

cards.name: Semillon
cards.blurb: A golden-hued grape often blended with Sauvignon Blanc, producing waxy whites with lemon curd and lanolin notes.

cards.name: Mourvèdre
cards.blurb: A meaty and herbal red grape that produces full-bodied wines with game, black fruit, and herb flavors.

cards.name: Barbera
cards.blurb: A juicy and high-acid Italian grape that produces everyday drinking wines with sour cherry and herb flavors.

cards.name: Pinot Gris
cards.blurb: A mutation of Pinot Noir that produces white wines ranging from zesty Italian Pinot Grigio to rich Alsatian styles.

cards.name: Petit Verdot
cards.blurb: A late-ripening Bordeaux blending grape that adds violet aromas and deep color to wines.

cards.name: Carmenère
cards.blurb: Once thought extinct in Bordeaux, this lost grape found a new home in Chile where it produces distinctive wines.

cards.name: Torrontés
cards.blurb: Argentina's signature white grape that smells sweet but tastes dry, often deceiving the senses.

cards.name: Moscato
cards.blurb: One of the world's oldest grape families, known for its sweet, fizzy, and intensely aromatic wines.

cards.name: Gewürztraminer
cards.blurb: A highly aromatic grape with distinctive lychee and rose petal aromas that is unmistakable in blind tastings.

cards.name: Albariño
cards.blurb: Spain's coastal Atlantic white grape that produces crisp, refreshing wines with apricot and sea salt notes.

cards.name: Grüner Veltliner
cards.blurb: Austria's pride and most planted grape, known for its distinctive white pepper and green pea notes.

cards.name: Vermentino
cards.blurb: A Mediterranean white grape that thrives along coastal regions, producing citrus-driven wines with herbal hints.

cards.name: Verdejo
cards.blurb: An aromatic Spanish white grape that produces herbal wines with fennel and grapefruit characteristics.

cards.name: Roussanne
cards.blurb: A golden Rhône white grape that produces full-bodied wines with herbal tea and pear flavors.

cards.name: Marsanne
cards.blurb: A rich white Rhône grape that produces nutty, full-bodied wines with almond and marzipan notes.

cards.name: Trebbiano
cards.blurb: A light and neutral Italian workhorse grape that produces high-volume, everyday white wines.

cards.name: Fiano
cards.blurb: An aromatic Italian white grape from Campania that produces wines with hazelnut and honey notes.

cards.name: Assyrtiko
cards.blurb: A Greek grape from Santorini with intense mineral character and very high acidity.

cards.name: Aglianico
cards.blurb: A powerful Italian red grape from southern Italy producing tannic, age-worthy wines with plum and leather notes.

cards.name: Nero d'Avola
cards.blurb: Sicily's most important red grape, producing rich wines with black cherry, plum, and spice flavors.

cards.name: Touriga Nacional
cards.blurb: Portugal's noblest grape and the backbone of Port wine, producing intensely colored wines with violet and dark fruit notes.

cards.name: Tannat
cards.blurb: A tannic powerhouse grape that has become Uruguay's national variety.

cards.name: Furmint
cards.blurb: The primary grape of Hungary's famous Tokaji sweet wines with very high acidity and citrus notes.

cards.name: Marselan
cards.blurb: A 1961 INRA crossing of Cabernet Sauvignon and Grenache, bred at Marseillan on the French coast and largely ignored there — then adopted by

cards.name: Cabernet Gernischt
cards.blurb: Not a variety of its own: DNA has confirmed that the vine China grows under this name is Carmenère, carried from Bordeaux to Shandong in the

cards.name: Koshu
cards.blurb: Japan's signature pale-purple skinned grape that yields delicate, mineral-driven whites.

cards.name: Muscat Bailey A
cards.blurb: A hybrid created in Japan combining Muscat of Hamburg and Bailey, producing aromatic, softly tannic reds with strawberry candy notes.

cards.name: Saperavi
cards.blurb: Georgia's flagship teinturier red with intense black fruit, savory spice, and the structure to age gracefully.

cards.name: Rkatsiteli
cards.blurb: Ancient Georgian white grape famed for amber qvevri wines with quince, tea, and honeyed depth.

cards.name: Kisi
cards.blurb: Fragrant Georgian white offering apricot, white flowers, and subtle tannin when fermented on skins.

cards.name: Dolcetto
cards.blurb: A Piedmontese red grape known for juicy black fruit, low acidity, and soft tannins, making it ideal for early drinking.

cards.name: Pinotage
cards.blurb: South Africa's signature crossing of Pinot Noir and Cinsault, producing deeply colored wines with dark berry fruit, smoke, and earthy spice.

cards.name: Montepulciano
cards.blurb: A widely planted central Italian red grape that gives plush, fruit-forward wines with moderate tannin and herbal depth.

cards.name: Corvina
cards.blurb: The principal red grape of Valpolicella, prized for sour-cherry brightness and herbal lift.

cards.name: Rondinella
cards.blurb: A reliable blending grape from Veneto commonly paired with Corvina in Valpolicella and Amarone.

cards.name: Pinot Blanc
cards.blurb: A white mutation of Pinot Noir producing crisp wines with orchard fruit, almond, and gentle floral notes.

cards.name: Pinot Meunier
cards.blurb: A key Champagne grape that brings ripe fruit, approachability, and early charm to sparkling blends.

cards.name: Petite Sirah
cards.blurb: A deeply colored, full-bodied red grape known for bold blackberry fruit, pepper, and firm tannins.

cards.name: Palomino
cards.blurb: The principal white grape of Jerez, valued for its neutral profile and ability to transmit the effects of biological and oxidative aging in Sherry.

cards.name: Baga
cards.blurb: Portugal's structured red grape from Bairrada, producing high-acid, high-tannin wines with dark berries, tobacco, and earthy complexity.

cards.name: Teroldego
cards.blurb: An alpine red from Trentino known for vivid color, dark berry fruit, and firm but polished tannins.

cards.name: Lagrein
cards.blurb: A deeply pigmented grape from Alto Adige producing structured wines with blackberry, cocoa, and smoky spice.

cards.name: Aligoté
cards.blurb: Burgundy's bright, high-acid white grape offering lemon, green apple, and chalky mineral notes.

cards.name: Melon de Bourgogne
cards.blurb: The grape behind Muscadet, the Loire's seafood white — every bottle of Muscadet is Melon de Bourgogne.

cards.name: Xinomavro
cards.blurb: Greece's age-worthy northern red known for high acidity, firm tannins, and aromas of sour cherry, olive, and sun-dried tomato.

cards.name: Agiorgitiko
cards.blurb: A versatile Greek red from Nemea producing plush wines with red berry fruit, warm spice, and supple tannins.

cards.name: Glera
cards.blurb: The principal grape of Prosecco, prized for fresh pear, apple, and white blossom aromas with lively but gentle acidity.

cards.name: Carignan
cards.blurb: A Mediterranean red grape known for deep color, savory dark fruit, and naturally high acidity.

cards.name: Cinsault
cards.blurb: A soft, aromatic red grape prized for red-fruit perfume and supple tannins.

cards.name: Falanghina
cards.blurb: A southern Italian white grape delivering bright citrus, apple, and floral aromas with refreshing acidity.

cards.name: Verdicchio
cards.blurb: A classic central Italian white grape known for citrus zest, bitter-almond finish, and subtle saline minerality.

cards.name: Müller-Thurgau
cards.blurb: A crossing of Riesling and Madeleine Royale that produces aromatic, easy-drinking whites with gentle acidity.

cards.name: Silvaner
cards.blurb: A traditional Central European white grape offering understated aromatics, savory texture, and marked site expression.

cards.name: Godello
cards.blurb: A rising Spanish white grape from Galicia and Bierzo with citrus, orchard fruit, and mineral depth.

cards.name: Verdelho
cards.blurb: A versatile white grape associated with Madeira and Australian coastal regions, showing tropical citrus, herbal hints, and bright freshness.

cards.name: Arinto
cards.blurb: A Portuguese white grape prized for naturally high acidity and citrus-mineral precision, even in warm climates.

cards.name: Zweigelt
cards.blurb: Austria's most planted red grape, combining juicy cherry fruit with peppery spice and bright acidity.

cards.name: Blaufränkisch
cards.blurb: A central European red with vivid acidity, dark berry fruit and a spicy, mineral edge, capable of real age in cooler sites.

cards.name: Nerello Mascalese
cards.blurb: Sicily's Etna flagship red, delivering pale color but firm structure with red fruit, herbs, and volcanic minerality.

cards.name: Primitivo
cards.blurb: A warm-climate red grape known for ripe black fruit, jammy richness, and generous alcohol.

cards.name: Friulano
cards.blurb: A northeastern Italian white grape with citrus, almond, and subtle herbal notes, often textured and dry.

cards.name: Fer Servadou
cards.blurb: A southwest French red grape valued for brisk acidity, black fruit, and peppery herbal character.

cards.name: Moschofilero
cards.blurb: An aromatic Greek pink-skinned grape used for fragrant white wines with rose, citrus, and spice notes.

cards.name: Pedro Ximénez
cards.blurb: The sherry grape behind the world's darkest dessert wine, sun-dried on mats until its juice pours like syrup.

cards.name: Ribolla Gialla
cards.blurb: A Friulian white with bright acidity and a citrus-and-flowers profile that turns golden and textural with skin contact.

cards.name: Savagnin
cards.blurb: Jura's ancient white grape, famous for Vin Jaune aged for years under a veil of yeast into something nutty, saline and unforgettable.

cards.name: Touriga Franca
cards.blurb: The Douro's most planted grape and the perfumed, supple counterpart to Touriga Nacional in Port blends.

cards.name: Frappato
cards.blurb: Sicily's brightest red: pale, perfumed and strawberry-fresh, often blended with Nero d'Avola in Cerasuolo di Vittoria.

cards.name: Garganega
cards.blurb: The grape of Soave, giving dry whites of pear, almond and white blossom from volcanic hills east of Verona.

cards.name: Graciano
cards.blurb: Rioja's seasoning grape: low-yielding, intensely aromatic, and prized for the acidity and violet lift it brings to Tempranillo blends.

cards.name: Greco
cards.blurb: An ancient Campanian white, at its peak in Greco di Tufo: stony, peachy and firm, with more grip than most Italian whites.

cards.name: Grillo
cards.blurb: Sicily's sun-proof white, once the backbone of Marsala and now the island's crisp, grapefruit-and-jasmine seafood wine.

cards.name: Hárslevelű
cards.blurb: Tokaj's second grape, the linden-scented partner to Furmint in Aszú blends, adding honeyed perfume and spice to the world's oldest classified sweet wine.

cards.name: Lambrusco
cards.blurb: Emilia's family of sparkling red grapes, frothing violet-scented and sour-cherry dry — the real thing is a world away from the sweet export cliché.

cards.name: Loureiro
cards.blurb: The laurel-scented white of Vinho Verde's Lima valley, all citrus blossom, bay leaf and Atlantic salt.

cards.name: Negroamaro
cards.blurb: Puglia's 'black and bitter' grape, though the wines are more plush than the name warns: dark cherry, dried herbs and a savory, faintly saline finish.

cards.name: Poulsard
cards.blurb: A ghost-pale Jura red with barely more pigment than a rosé, trading power for perfume: pomegranate, rose and forest floor.

cards.name: Trousseau
cards.blurb: The sturdier of Jura's two red grapes, giving translucent wines with red cherry, pepper and a woodland earthiness.

cards.name: Vidal
cards.blurb: A thick-skinned French hybrid that found its destiny frozen solid on Canadian vines: Vidal icewine pours apricot, honey and tropical fruit over electric acidity.

cards.name: Chinuri
cards.blurb: Kartli's high-valley white, picked late for sparkling wine and vinified fresh or in qvevri for the table.

cards.name: Goruli Mtsvane
cards.blurb: Kartli's own 'green' grape, distinct from Kakheti's Mtsvane, bringing quince, white flowers and stony freshness to still and sparkling wines alike.

cards.name: Mtsvane
cards.blurb: Kakheti's aromatic white, often married to Rkatsiteli in qvevri for perfume the sturdier grape lacks.

cards.name: Otskhanuri Sapere
cards.blurb: Imereti's rare, deeply colored red, fermented in clay churi for wines of sour cherry bite, violet lift and wild-country earth.

cards.name: Tsolikouri
cards.blurb: Western Georgia's workhorse white, brighter and leaner than Kakheti's amber giants, with pear, honeyed blossom and wet-stone minerality.

cards.name: Romorantin
cards.blurb: The only grape of tiny Cour-Cheverny, planted in the Loire on the orders of François I five centuries ago and grown nowhere else on earth.

cards.name: Pineau d'Aunis
cards.blurb: A medieval Loire red once poured for Plantagenet kings, now a handful of hectares of peppery, kirsch-pale wine.

cards.name: Vaccarèse
cards.blurb: One of Châteauneuf-du-Pape's forgotten thirteen, kept alive by a few faithful estates for the floral lift it lends Grenache.

cards.name: Muscardin
cards.blurb: The rarest of Châteauneuf's authorized varieties, down to a scatter of rows across the whole appellation.

cards.name: Terret Noir
cards.blurb: An old Languedoc vine that earned one of Châteauneuf's thirteen seats for the acidity and herbal snap it brings to sun-heavy blends.

cards.name: Picardan
cards.blurb: Châteauneuf-du-Pape's least-planted white, a discreet salted-lemon seasoning surviving on single rows kept for the appellation's honor.

cards.name: Picpoul
cards.blurb: The 'lip-stinger' of the Languedoc coast, all screaming citrus and salt, built for oyster beds an hour away.

cards.name: Counoise
cards.blurb: The southern Rhône's quiet seasoning grape, prized in Châteauneuf blends for plummy fruit, pepper and acidity that Grenache burns off.

cards.name: Clairette
cards.blurb: One of the Rhône's oldest whites, blossomy and low in acid, long used to soften and perfume southern blends.

cards.name: Bourboulenc
cards.blurb: A late-ripening Mediterranean white threaded through the southern Rhône and Languedoc, bringing citrus and a saline snap to blends that woul

cards.name: Pelaverga
cards.blurb: Verduno's own pale-ruby secret, a single village's grape making strawberry-and-white-pepper reds beside some of Barolo's grandest crus.

cards.name: Ruché
cards.blurb: Castagnole Monferrato's aromatic red riddle: rose-petal perfume over dark cherry, from a grape legend says a monk carried over the Alps.

cards.name: Timorasso
cards.blurb: Rescued from a few abandoned rows in the Colli Tortonesi, Piedmont's great lost white makes dense, mineral wines that age like fine Riesling.

cards.name: Nascetta
cards.blurb: The village of Novello's half-forgotten white, once vinified sweet for special occasions and revived dry only in the 1990s.

cards.name: Vespaiolo
cards.blurb: Breganze's high-acid white, named for the wasps that mob its sugar-rich berries at harvest.

cards.name: Pignolo
cards.blurb: Friuli's sternest red, saved from two surviving vines against an abbey wall in the 1970s.

cards.name: Sagrantino
cards.blurb: Montefalco's ferocious red, holder of the highest tannin levels of any major grape, once made only as a sacramental sweet wine.

cards.name: Grignolino
cards.blurb: Piedmont's contrarian: a pale, nervy red with prominent tannin from its many pips — the name derives from dialect for them.

cards.name: Pignoletto
cards.blurb: Bologna's own frothy white from the Colli Bolognesi, almost always lightly sparkling and poured beside mortadella.

cards.name: Schioppettino
cards.blurb: A Friulian border red that 'crackles' on the tongue — the name says so — rescued by one village's petition after phylloxera nearly ended it.

cards.name: Carricante
cards.blurb: Etna's ancient white, grown up the volcano's eastern slope where a thousand metres of altitude keep its acidity electric.

cards.name: Hondarrabi Zuri
cards.blurb: The white grape of Txakoli, poured theatrically from height into tumblers along the Basque coast.

cards.name: Hondarrabi Beltza
cards.blurb: The red of the Basque coast, mostly vinified into rosé-pink, faintly fizzy Txakoli or brisk, crunchy reds served cool.

cards.name: Xarel·lo
cards.blurb: The backbone of Cava and the most structured of its trio, increasingly bottled alone as Catalonia's serious still white.

cards.name: Bobal
cards.blurb: Spain's secret workhorse — long the country's second most planted red, almost none of it ever labeled.

cards.name: Mencía
cards.blurb: The perfumed red of Spain's misty northwest, remade in a generation from jug wine into Bierzo's graphite-edged answer to fine Burgundy.

cards.name: Trepat
cards.blurb: Conca de Barberà's pale local red, long hidden inside rosé Cava and only recently trusted with its own label.

cards.name: Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains
cards.blurb: The oldest and finest of the Muscat family, the rare grape whose wine actually smells of the grape itself.

cards.name: Grenache Blanc
cards.blurb: The white workhorse of the southern Rhône and Roussillon: fleshy, low-acid and quietly herbal, the padding in countless white blends.

cards.name: Colombard
cards.blurb: Gascony's crisp everyday white, once distilled into Armagnac and now poured young, cold and unapologetically simple.

cards.name: Mondeuse
cards.blurb: Savoie's peppery mountain red, deep-coloured and wiry, tasting of dark cherries rolled in cracked pepper.

cards.name: Négrette
cards.blurb: The floral dark grape of Fronton, north of Toulouse, making supple violet-scented reds almost nowhere else on earth.

cards.name: Jacquère
cards.blurb: The featherweight white of Savoie's ski villages, grown under limestone peaks and drunk within sight of them.

cards.name: Cortese
cards.blurb: The grape behind Gavi, Piedmont's coolly precise white — pale, citrus-edged and faintly bitter-almond at the finish.

cards.name: Arneis
cards.blurb: Roero's 'little rascal', a white so tricky to grow that Piedmont nearly let it die out in the 1960s.

cards.name: Pecorino
cards.blurb: Not the cheese: a sharp-boned mountain white from the Marche and Abruzzo, named for the sheep that grazed its hillsides.

cards.name: Vernaccia
cards.blurb: The white of San Gimignano's towers, praised by Dante and licensed as Italy's first DOC in 1966.

cards.name: Catarratto
cards.blurb: Sicily's most-planted grape, long boiled down anonymously for Marsala and vermouth, now bottled on its own terms.

cards.name: Cesanese
cards.blurb: Lazio's own red, grown in the hills southeast of Rome since imperial times and mostly drunk before it ever reaches the city gates.

cards.name: Airén
cards.blurb: The quiet giant of La Mancha's endless plateau — for decades the most-planted wine grape on earth, and almost nobody outside Spain has heard of it.

cards.name: Macabeo
cards.blurb: Rioja calls it Viura and makes its whites from it; Penedès calls it Macabeo and puts it in the Cava trio with Xarel·lo and Parellada.

cards.name: Parellada
cards.blurb: The finesse of the Cava trio, grown highest on the Penedès slopes and picked first.

cards.name: Garnacha Blanca
cards.blurb: Grenache Blanc under its home flag: Spain's fleshy white Garnacha, at its grandest in Terra Alta's old bush vines and a quiet stiffener in white Rioja.

cards.name: Listán Negro
cards.blurb: The volcanic red of the Canary Islands, trained in braided cordons across black ash fields that never knew phylloxera.

cards.name: Treixadura
cards.blurb: Ribeiro's aristocrat, the peach-and-blossom white of Galicia's oldest wine valley, usually leading a local field blend.

cards.name: Abouriou
cards.blurb: A Garonne-valley red that ripens before anything around it and tastes like it was picked in a hurry — brisk, peppery, light on tannin.

cards.name: Alicante Bouschet
cards.blurb: Henri Bouschet’s 1855 crossing of Petit Bouschet and Grenache, and the rare teinturier whose flesh runs as red as its skin — a grape bred to

cards.name: Alfrocheiro
cards.blurb: A Dão native that lends colour and blackberry depth to blends most drinkers never see it named in.

cards.name: Arinto dos Açores
cards.blurb: The Azores’ own white, unrelated to mainland Arinto and called Terrantez da Terceira until a 2012 decree settled the name.

cards.name: Babić
cards.blurb: Dalmatia’s stony red, grown on the terraced karst above Primošten in vineyards so laboriously walled that a photograph of them hangs at the United Nations.

cards.name: Brancellao
cards.blurb: A pale, perfumed Galician red that gives almost no colour and an enormous amount of scent — rose and raspberry on a frame you can see through.

cards.name: Cabernet Pfeffer
cards.blurb: Under twenty acres survive, most of them old vines in San Benito and the Santa Clara Valley, and UC Davis has settled what they are: Mourtao

cards.name: Caíño Tinto
cards.blurb: The sharpest of the Caíño family, and the one people mean when they just say Caíño: late, thick-skinned and so acidic that growers spent decades pulling it out.

cards.name: Callet
cards.blurb: Mallorca’s soft-spoken red, pale and low in alcohol in a place where neither is expected.

cards.name: Canaiolo
cards.blurb: Chianti’s old second grape, written into Ricasoli’s nineteenth-century formula to soften Sangiovese’s edges and then quietly replaced by French varieties.

cards.name: Castelão
cards.blurb: Portugal’s great southern workhorse, known as Periquita after the vineyard that first bottled it.

cards.name: Colorino
cards.blurb: A Tuscan teinturier kept for exactly one purpose — colour — and blended in at a few percent to darken Chianti.

cards.name: Corvinone
cards.blurb: Long assumed to be a big-berried Corvina and shown by DNA to be nothing of the kind.

cards.name: Croatina
cards.blurb: Italian despite the name, and confusingly sold as Bonarda in the Oltrepò Pavese — which has nothing to do with Argentina’s Bonarda.

cards.name: Espadeiro
cards.blurb: A Vinho Verde red grown for rosé more often than for red wine, all sharp raspberry and no weight at all.

cards.name: Freisa
cards.blurb: A confirmed child of Nebbiolo — the relationship was read the other way round until 2020 — and Piedmont’s most divisive grape: strawberry an

cards.name: Grolleau
cards.blurb: The Loire’s rosé engine, planted by the thousand hectares for Rosé d’Anjou and almost never named on a label.

cards.name: Negramoll
cards.blurb: Madeira’s real workhorse, behind the great majority of the island’s wine while Sercial and Verdelho take the credit.

cards.name: Nerello Cappuccio
cards.blurb: Etna’s other Nerello, named for the hood its canopy throws over the fruit, and no relation to Mascalese — nerello is only dialect for a dark-berried vine.

cards.name: País
cards.blurb: The grape Spain carried to the Americas: Listán Prieto at home, Mission in California, Criolla Chica in Argentina, País in Chile.

cards.name: Sciaccarellu
cards.blurb: Corsica’s peppery red, and the same variety Tuscany calls Mammolo — an identity France’s official catalogue records from both ampelographic

cards.name: St. Laurent
cards.blurb: A dark, cherry-scented Austrian red, and a child of Pinot Noir rather than a clone of it — the second parent has never been found.

cards.name: Sumoll
cards.blurb: A Catalan red down to its last few dozen hectares, pulled out across the twentieth century for the crime of not making Cava.

cards.name: Valdiguié
cards.blurb: Sold in California as Napa Gamay for decades before anyone checked, at which point it turned out to be a declining Languedoc bulk grape with

cards.name: Vinhão
cards.blurb: The red that stains the glass: a Minho teinturier making the near-black, teeth-rasping vinho verde tinto that outsiders almost never meet.

cards.name: Sercial
cards.blurb: The driest rung of the Madeira ladder and the last of the noble whites to ripen, grown high and cold enough that the acidity never softens.

cards.name: Boal
cards.blurb: Madeira's medium-rich style, picked lower and warmer than Sercial and sweeter by exactly that margin, with a nutty marmalade weight behind the island acidity.

cards.name: Malvasia de São Jorge
cards.blurb: The grape behind Malmsey, the sweetest and darkest rung of the Madeira ladder, all coffee, dried fig and burnt sugar cut by acidity that refuses to let it cloy.

cards.name: Gouais Blanc
cards.blurb: The most important grape almost nobody drinks: crossed with Pinot it fathered Chardonnay, Gamay and Aligoté, and its confirmed children run

cards.name: Plavac Mali
cards.blurb: Dalmatia's flagship red, worked by hand on coastal slopes too steep for a tractor, giving dark, high-alcohol wines of dried fig, pepper and sea air.

cards.name: Manto Negro
cards.blurb: Mallorca's principal red and the island's own, pale in the glass and low in acid, built for drinking young rather than keeping.

cards.name: Mavrud
cards.blurb: Bulgaria’s great native red, at home around Asenovgrad on the warm Thracian plain: late-ripening, thick-skinned, and dark enough that its na

cards.name: Melnik
cards.blurb: Shorthand for Shiroka Melnishka Loza — Broad-Leaved Melnik — grown in the hot Struma corridor and effectively nowhere else on earth.

cards.name: Obaideh
cards.blurb: Lebanon’s ancient white, grown own-rooted on the Bekaa and Batroun heights and spent most of its history being distilled into arak.

cards.name: Merwah
cards.blurb: The other half of Lebanon’s white story, hanging on in high Mount Lebanon vineyards above Batroun where some ungrafted vines are counted in

cards.name: Zelen
cards.blurb: Named for the green glint it leaves in the glass and grown only in the upper Vipava Valley, where Valvasor’s chronicle already recorded it in 1689.

cards.name: Pinela
cards.blurb: Vipava’s other endemic white, documented in the valley back to the fourteenth century and now down to a few dozen hectares of delicate, apple-and-blossom wine.

cards.name: Chasselas

cards.name: Teran
cards.blurb: The iron-edged red of the terra rossa: sour cherry, game and graphite over acidity that takes no prisoners.

cards.name: Fetească Regală
cards.blurb: Romania’s royal white, spotted in a Transylvanian nursery around 1920 and named for the crown in 1928.

cards.name: Savatiano
cards.blurb: The most planted grape in Greece and the workhorse of Attica, so drought-hardy it shrugs off the driest summers in the country.

cards.name: Malagousia
cards.blurb: A grape that nearly vanished: down to a few vines in the 1970s when a professor at Thessaloniki and the winemakers of Porto Carras coaxed it back.

cards.name: Mavrodaphne
cards.blurb: The dark laurel of the Peloponnese, best known fortified: sweet Mavrodaphne of Patras ages for years in old casks toward coffee, fig and bitter chocolate.

cards.name: Encruzado
cards.blurb: The great white of the Dão, grown almost nowhere else, and Portugal’s strongest answer to white Burgundy.

cards.name: Fernão Pires
cards.blurb: Portugal’s most planted white grape, filling the warm river plains of the Tejo and, as Maria Gomes, leading Bairrada’s still and sparkling whites.

cards.name: Altesse
cards.blurb: Savoie’s noblest white, sold as Roussette de Savoie and named for the russet blush its ripe berries take on.

cards.name: Petite Arvine
cards.blurb: The flagship native of the Valais, clinging to terraces above the young Rhône and found almost nowhere outside Switzerland.

cards.name: Kadarka
cards.blurb: The old red of the Pannonian lands, once the backbone of Eger’s Bikáver and still Bulgaria’s Gamza.

cards.name: Dornfelder
cards.blurb: Germany’s modern red success: bred by August Herold at Weinsberg in 1955 and now the country’s second most planted dark grape.

cards.blurb: Georg Scheu’s 1916 crossing from Alzey, grown in Rheinhessen and the Pfalz and prized where Riesling structure meets blackcurrant-and-grapefruit exuberance.

cards.name: Fetească Neagră
cards.blurb: Romania’s great native red, documented for centuries around Uricani in Moldavia and revived from near-extinction after the phylloxera and Soviet eras.

cards.name: Xynisteri
cards.blurb: Cyprus’s dominant white, grown ungrafted on an island phylloxera never reached, and half of every true Commandaria.

cards.name: Mavro
cards.blurb: The black grape of Cyprus, so long the island’s default that its name is simply the Greek for black.

cards.name: Gaglioppo
cards.blurb: Calabria’s standard-bearer and the grape of Cirò, grown on the coastal shelf where Greek settlers planted some of Italy’s first vines.

cards.name: Nosiola
cards.blurb: Trentino’s only native white, named for the hazelnut its wines taste of, grown between the Dolomites and Lake Garda.

cards.name: Marquette
cards.blurb: A French-American hybrid, not a vinifera: bred at the University of Minnesota and released in 2006 to survive winters that kill European vines outright.

cards.name: Boğazkere
cards.blurb: The throat burner — the name is a fair warning.

cards.name: Burgundy
cards.blurb: The spiritual home of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, where terroir is expressed with unmatched precision.

cards.name: Champagne
cards.blurb: The only region that can legally produce true Champagne, using the traditional method of secondary fermentation in bottle.

cards.name: Rhône Valley
cards.blurb: A sun-drenched region divided into the elegant Northern Rhône and the broader Southern Rhône.

cards.name: Loire Valley
cards.blurb: Known as the Garden of France, this diverse region stretches along the Loire River.

cards.name: Alsace
cards.blurb: A unique French region with Germanic influence, known for its aromatic white wines in distinctive tall bottles.

cards.name: Provence
cards.blurb: The world's most famous rosé-producing region, blessed with Mediterranean sunshine and maritime breezes.

cards.name: Beaujolais
cards.blurb: The home of Gamay grape, producing bright, fruity wines that range from simple Nouveau to age-worthy Cru wines.

cards.name: Languedoc
cards.blurb: France's largest wine region, offering exceptional value and increasingly high quality wines.

cards.name: Chablis
cards.blurb: A northern outpost of Burgundy famous for mineral, unoaked Chardonnay that expresses pure chalky terroir.

cards.name: Sauternes
cards.blurb: The world's most celebrated sweet wine region, where noble rot transforms Sémillon and Sauvignon Blanc into liquid gold.

cards.name: Jura
cards.blurb: A quirky French region known for its unique oxidative wines like Vin Jaune and distinctive local grapes.

cards.name: Napa Valley
cards.blurb: America's most prestigious wine region, known for powerful Cabernet Sauvignon that rivals Bordeaux.

cards.name: Sonoma
cards.blurb: Napa's diverse coastal neighbor, producing excellent wines from numerous varieties across varied microclimates.

cards.name: Willamette Valley
cards.blurb: Oregon's cool-climate paradise for Pinot Noir, producing elegant wines that rival Burgundy.

cards.name: Paso Robles
cards.blurb: California's hub for Rhône varieties, producing bold Syrahs and GSM blends in a warm, inland climate.

cards.name: Walla Walla
cards.blurb: Washington State's premium wine valley, known for elegant Syrah and refined Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.name: Santa Barbara
cards.blurb: Cool-climate California wine country made famous by the film Sideways.

cards.name: Finger Lakes
cards.blurb: New York State's premier wine region, producing world-class Riesling from steep lakeside vineyards.

cards.name: Lodi
cards.blurb: California's treasure trove of old vine Zinfandel, some over 100 years old.

cards.name: Tuscany
cards.blurb: Italy's most beloved wine region, where Sangiovese reigns supreme across varied terroirs.

cards.name: Piedmont
cards.blurb: The home of Nebbiolo, producing Italy's greatest red wines including Barolo and Barbaresco.

cards.name: Veneto
cards.blurb: Italy's most productive wine region, home to Prosecco, Amarone, and Soave.

cards.name: Sicily
cards.blurb: Italy's largest wine island, producing increasingly impressive wines from ancient native varieties.

cards.name: Campania
cards.blurb: Southern Italy's jewel of ancient grape varieties grown on volcanic soils near Naples.

cards.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
cards.blurb: Italy's top region for premium white wines, bordering Slovenia and Austria.

cards.name: Alto Adige
cards.blurb: A bilingual Italian-German region in the Alps producing fresh, aromatic white wines.

cards.name: Abruzzo
cards.blurb: Central Italy's workhorse region, famous for value-driven Montepulciano d'Abruzzo.

cards.name: Puglia
cards.blurb: The heel of Italy's boot, producing bold, fruity reds from Primitivo and Negroamaro.

cards.name: Rioja
cards.blurb: Spain's most famous wine region, known for Tempranillo-based wines aged in American oak.

cards.name: Ribera del Duero
cards.blurb: High-altitude wine country producing powerful, concentrated Tempranillo wines.

cards.name: Priorat
cards.blurb: A dramatic region of ancient slate soils producing intensely concentrated wines.

cards.name: Rías Baixas
cards.blurb: Spain's premier white wine region on the Atlantic coast of Galicia.

cards.name: Rueda
cards.blurb: Spain's answer to Sauvignon Blanc country, producing crisp, herbal whites from Verdejo.

cards.name: Jerez
cards.blurb: The birthplace of Sherry, producing unique fortified wines through solera aging.

cards.name: Douro
cards.blurb: Portugal's great river valley, home to Port wine and increasingly impressive dry reds.

cards.name: Vinho Verde
cards.blurb: Portugal's refreshing white wine region producing light, crisp wines with a slight spritz.

cards.name: Mosel
cards.blurb: Germany's most famous wine region, producing ethereal Rieslings from impossibly steep slate slopes.

cards.name: Rheingau
cards.blurb: A historic German region where noble Riesling was first cultivated for dry wines.

cards.name: Wachau
cards.blurb: Austria's most prestigious wine region along the Danube River, producing world-class Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.

cards.name: Barossa Valley
cards.blurb: Australia's most famous wine region, home to century-old Shiraz vines producing powerful, rich wines.

cards.name: Margaret River
cards.blurb: Western Australia's premium region producing Bordeaux-style blends and elegant Chardonnay.

cards.name: Marlborough
cards.blurb: New Zealand's largest and most famous region, producing intensely aromatic Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.name: Central Otago
cards.blurb: The world's southernmost wine region, producing exceptional Pinot Noir at high altitude.

cards.name: Mendoza
cards.blurb: Argentina's wine heartland at the foot of the Andes, where high-altitude vineyards produce world-class Malbec.

cards.name: Maipo Valley
cards.blurb: Chile's most prestigious wine valley, known for powerful Cabernet Sauvignon.

cards.name: Stellenbosch
cards.blurb: South Africa's premier wine region, producing world-class Cabernet Sauvignon and unique Pinotage.

cards.name: Santorini
cards.blurb: A Greek island of volcanic vineyards producing intensely mineral Assyrtiko.

cards.name: Tokaj
cards.blurb: Hungary's legendary region producing Tokaji Aszú, one of the world's great sweet wines.

cards.name: Helan Mountain
cards.blurb: China's flagship high-desert wine frontier in Ningxia, producing polished Bordeaux-style reds under dramatic rocky ridges.

cards.name: Shangri-La
cards.blurb: Sky-high vineyards perched along the Mekong in Yunnan, delivering perfumed reds with alpine freshness from ancient terraces.

cards.name: Yamanashi
cards.blurb: Japan's Kōshu Valley beneath Mount Fuji, home to delicate Koshu whites and experimental sparkling wines with pristine acidity.

cards.name: Nashik
cards.blurb: India's wine capital north of Mumbai, where breezy plateaus yield tropical-leaning whites and peppery Syrah.

cards.name: Nandi Hills
cards.blurb: Cooler Karnataka hill country that lends lift and spice to India's premium Syrah and Cabernet bottlings.

cards.name: Swartland
cards.blurb: Swartland's old bush vines and granite soils craft textured Chenin Blanc and soulful Rhône-style reds with minimal intervention.

cards.name: Walker Bay
cards.blurb: A cool, ocean-swept corner famed for Hemel-en-Aarde Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, delivering Burgundian elegance with South African sunshine.

cards.name: Paarl & Franschhoek
cards.blurb: Historic valleys east of Stellenbosch producing rich reds, fynbos-scented whites, and South Africa's marquee Cap Classique sparklers.

cards.name: Kakheti
cards.blurb: Georgia's eastern cradle of wine, famous for skin-contact amber wines and powerful Saperavi reds fermented in buried qvevri.

cards.name: Kartli
cards.blurb: Highland vineyards near Tbilisi yielding elegant sparkling Chinuri and balanced qvevri whites with alpine freshness.

cards.name: Imereti
cards.blurb: Western Georgia's humid hills where partial qvevri fermentations craft brighter, mineral-driven amber and red wines.

cards.name: Burgenland
cards.blurb: Austria's red-wine country along the Hungarian border, where the shallow Neusiedlersee stretches the season for Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt.

cards.name: Niederösterreich
cards.blurb: Lower Austria, the country's largest wine region, wrapping the Danube valleys and the vast Weinviertel.

cards.name: Canary Islands

cards.name: Naoussa

cards.name: Amyndeon
cards.blurb: Greece's highest and coolest appellation, on a lake-moderated plateau where Xinomavro turns bright, floral and fine-boned.

cards.name: Sardinia
cards.blurb: A granite island with its own grape lexicon: Vermentino di Gallura on the windy north coast, old-vine Cannonau inland, Carignano in the sandy southwest.

cards.name: Trentino
cards.blurb: Alpine northern Italy along the Adige, split between mountain whites and the native Teroldego on the gravelly Campo Rotaliano.

cards.name: Valpolicella
cards.blurb: The Veneto's cherry-red heartland north of Verona, where Corvina and Rondinella range from light and fresh to the dried-grape monuments of Amarone.

cards.name: Emilia-Romagna
cards.blurb: Italy's food belt between the Po and the Apennines, washing Parmigiano and prosciutto down with dry, foaming Lambrusco.

cards.name: Etna
cards.blurb: Vineyards climb the active volcano to nearly a thousand metres, where Nerello Mascalese reads more like alpine Pinot than Sicilian red.

cards.name: Collio
cards.blurb: A crescent of border hills between Friuli and Slovenia, Italy's benchmark for structured, site-driven whites.

cards.name: Shandong
cards.blurb: China's maritime wine coast, where the Yantai peninsula hosts the country's oldest modern wineries and most of its production.

cards.name: Hebei
cards.blurb: The vineyards ringing Beijing, from coastal Changli to the Huailai basin at altitude.

cards.name: Franconia
cards.blurb: Germany's Silvaner country along the Main, bottling dry, earthy whites in the squat round Bocksbeutel.

cards.name: Rheinhessen
cards.blurb: Germany's largest wine region, reinvented in a generation from bulk supplier to the engine room of the country's dry-Riesling avant-garde.

cards.name: Gaillac
cards.blurb: One of France's oldest vineyards, planted by the Romans on the Tarn, and a refuge for grapes that exist nowhere else.

cards.name: Hunter Valley
cards.blurb: Australia's oldest wine region and its most counterintuitive: subtropical heat producing featherweight, unoaked Semillon that ages for decades.

cards.name: Madeira

cards.name: Dão

cards.name: Alentejo
cards.blurb: The wide, cork-oak south of Portugal, where warm plains and clay-schist hills give generous, round reds led by Aragonez and Touriga Nacional.

cards.name: Valdeorras
cards.blurb: Galicia's inland valley of slate and sunlight, the source of Spain's most mineral Godello.

cards.blurb: Baja California's granite valley two hours south of the border, cooled by Pacific fog and unbound by appellation rules.

cards.name: Umbria

cards.blurb: The southern limit of Argentine wine, down the Río Negro and Neuquén valleys where desert wind thickens skins and cool nights preserve nerve.

cards.name: Codru
cards.blurb: Moldova’s central hills, where oak forests break the steppe wind and most of the country’s vast vineyard grows.

cards.name: Ștefan Vodă
cards.blurb: Moldova’s southeastern corner above the Dniester, home of Purcari, whose dark Negru blend won gold in Paris in 1878 and stocked the cellars

cards.name: Vayots Dzor
cards.blurb: A high mountain province of southern Armenia where vines grow ungrafted at 1,400 metres or more between volcanic outcrops and limestone gorges.

cards.name: Aragatsotn
cards.blurb: The volcanic apron of Mount Aragats northwest of Yerevan, dry, sun-hammered and irrigated from mountain snowmelt since Urartian times.

cards.name: Commandaria
cards.blurb: Fourteen villages on the south slopes of the Troodos, delimited for a single wine: the sun-dried amber sweet the Crusaders named for their commandery at Kolossi.

cards.name: Pitsilia
cards.blurb: Cyprus’s highest vineyards, terraced up the Troodos to 1,400 metres on an island phylloxera never reached.

cards.name: Styria
cards.blurb: Austria's green southeast, where vineyards climb hills steep enough to need winches and Sauvignon Blanc found a second homeland.

cards.name: Jurançon
cards.blurb: Pyrenean foothill terraces above Pau, delimited in 1936 among France's first AOCs and famous since a Manseng sweet was poured at Henri IV's baptism.

cards.name: Cappadocia
cards.blurb: A thousand-metre plateau of carved tuff where vineyards grow between fairy chimneys and wineries age their bottles in caves cut by hand.

cards.name: Elazığ
cards.blurb: High terraces above the dammed Euphrates in eastern Anatolia, the home vineyard of Öküzgözü and the upstream half of Turkey's classic red blend.

cards.name: Full-Body Red
cards.blurb: Rich, tannic wines with intense dark fruit flavors that command attention on the palate.

cards.name: Light-Body Red
cards.blurb: Delicate, elegant reds with bright acidity and fresh red fruit character that are perfect for lighter fare.

cards.name: Medium-Body Red
cards.blurb: Versatile reds that balance fruit, structure, and elegance for everyday enjoyment.

cards.name: Full-Body White
cards.blurb: Opulent white wines often with oak influence, offering rich texture and creamy mouthfeel.

cards.name: Light-Body White
cards.blurb: Crisp, refreshing whites with high acidity and clean, mineral-driven flavors.

cards.name: Aromatic White
cards.blurb: Intensely fragrant white wines with floral, fruity, and spicy aromas that leap from the glass.

cards.name: Rosé
cards.blurb: Refreshing pink wines made from red grapes with minimal skin contact.

cards.name: Sparkling Wine
cards.blurb: Effervescent wines with elegant bubbles created through secondary fermentation.

cards.name: Champagne
cards.blurb: The original and most prestigious sparkling wine, made only in the Champagne region of France.

cards.name: Dessert Wine
cards.blurb: Lusciously sweet wines crafted from super-ripe or dried grapes, perfect for ending a meal.

cards.name: Fortified Wine
cards.blurb: Wines strengthened with grape spirit to increase alcohol and preserve sweetness.

cards.name: Port
cards.blurb: Portugal's famous sweet fortified wine from the Douro Valley, made by adding brandy during fermentation.

cards.name: Sherry
cards.blurb: Spain's unique fortified wine from Jerez, aged in a solera system to create complex oxidative or biological styles.

cards.name: Natural Wine
cards.blurb: Low-intervention wines made with minimal additives and often without filtration.

cards.name: Orange Wine
cards.blurb: White grapes vinified like red wine, with extended skin contact creating amber color and tannic structure.

cards.name: Pétillant Naturel
cards.blurb: Naturally sparkling wines made using the ancestral method, bottled before primary fermentation completes.

cards.name: Late Harvest
cards.blurb: Sweet wines made from grapes left on the vine past normal harvest to concentrate sugar.

cards.name: Ice Wine
cards.blurb: Ultra-sweet wines made from grapes naturally frozen on the vine, concentrating sugars and acids.

cards.name: Botrytis Wine
cards.blurb: Noble rot sweet wines where Botrytis cinerea fungus concentrates grape sugars while adding honeyed complexity.

cards.name: GSM Blend
cards.blurb: Classic Rhône-style blend of Grenache, Syrah, and Mourvèdre creating complex, balanced reds.

cards.name: Bordeaux Blend
cards.blurb: Classic blend dominated by Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot with supporting varieties.

cards.name: Super Tuscan
cards.blurb: Non-traditional Italian wines that broke from DOC rules by blending international varieties with local grapes.

cards.name: Cru Beaujolais
cards.blurb: Age-worthy Gamay from the ten named villages of Beaujolais, offering serious wines beyond simple Nouveau.

cards.name: Crémant
cards.blurb: French sparkling wines made in the traditional method outside Champagne, offering excellent value.

cards.name: Prosecco
cards.blurb: Italy's most popular sparkling wine, made from Glera grapes using the tank method.

cards.name: Qvevri Amber
cards.blurb: Skin-contact whites fermented in buried clay qvevri, yielding tea-like tannin, dried orchard fruit, and honeyed spice.

cards.name: Chillable Red
cards.blurb: Light, low-tannin reds built for a chill, bursting with red fruit and peppery zest for warm-weather sipping.

cards.name: Sparkling Red
cards.blurb: Fizz meets dark fruit: from Lambrusco to sparkling Shiraz, these wines marry bubbles with berry-rich, savory depth.

cards.name: Noble Grapes
cards.blurb: A curated grouping of the NOBLE-tier varieties whose pedigree, structure, and complexity define the most prestigious styles.

cards.name: Medium-Body White
cards.blurb: White wines with real texture but no oak heaviness, sitting between crisp aperitif and full-blown richness.

cards.name: Sweet White
cards.blurb: Unabashedly sweet whites, from gently fizzy Moscato to syrup-dark Pedro Ximénez and frozen-vine Vidal icewine.

cards.name: Madeira
cards.blurb: Fortified wine from the Atlantic island, deliberately heated and oxidised until it is virtually indestructible - an opened bottle keeps for

cards.blurb: Spain's traditional-method sparkling wine, its second fermentation in the bottle and its heartland Penedès, built from the Catalan trio of M

cards.blurb: The Jura’s yellow wine: Savagnin aged at least six years and three months under a veil of yeast in barrels never topped up, then bottled in

cards.blurb: Hungary’s wine of kings: botrytis-shrivelled aszú berries picked one by one and steeped in base wine from the Tokaj hills, then aged in cell

cards.name: Retsina
cards.blurb: Greece’s resinated white, made by adding Aleppo pine resin to the fermenting must, a habit descended from the resin-sealed amphorae of antiq

cards.name: Passito
cards.blurb: Wines from grapes dried on mats, racks or rafters until the sugar concentrates, an Italian craft older than Rome.

cards.name: Marsala
cards.blurb: Sicily’s great fortified wine, born in 1773 when an English trader dosed a shipment with spirit to survive the voyage.

cards.name: Commandaria
cards.blurb: The oldest named wine still made: sun-dried Xynisteri and Mavro from fourteen villages on the Troodos foothills, aged for years in old casks

cards.name: Vinho Verde
cards.blurb: Portugal’s green wine is green as in young, not in colour: bottled months off the vine from the rainy Minho, light in alcohol, sharp with ac

cards.name: Blackcurrant
cards.blurb: Blackcurrant, also called cassis, is the small tart black berry of the currant bush, darker and more pungent than blackberry.

cards.name: Cedar
cards.blurb: Cedar is the dry, sweetly resinous scent of cedarwood, familiar from pencil boxes and cigar humidors.

cards.name: Spice
cards.blurb: Spice is a broad sweet-spice impression, cinnamon, clove and pepper blurred together rather than any one jar.

cards.name: Cherry
cards.blurb: Cherry is the bright note of fresh sweet cherries, the signature fruit of many mid-weight reds.

cards.name: Earth
cards.blurb: Earth is the smell of turned soil or a forest floor after rain.

cards.name: Floral
cards.blurb: Floral is a general flower-garden lift rather than any one identifiable bloom.

cards.name: Red Apple
cards.blurb: Red apple is the mellow, faintly sweet scent of a ripe dessert apple.

cards.name: Butter
cards.blurb: Butter is the rich, creamy scent of melted butter.

cards.name: Vanilla
cards.blurb: Vanilla is the sweet baking scent of vanilla pod.

cards.name: Plum
cards.blurb: Plum is the fleshy dark fruit note of ripe plums, rounder and softer than blackberry.

cards.name: Chocolate
cards.blurb: Chocolate is a sweet, rounded cocoa richness in the finish of a red wine.

cards.name: Herbs
cards.blurb: Herbs is the mixed green scent of a kitchen herb bundle, thyme, bay and their kin.

cards.name: Blackberry
cards.blurb: Blackberry is the deep, sweet-tart note of ripe bramble fruit.

cards.name: Pepper
cards.blurb: Pepper is the pungent bite of freshly cracked peppercorns.

cards.name: Smoke
cards.blurb: Smoke is the char and woodsmoke edge some reds carry.

cards.name: Lime
cards.blurb: Lime is the sharp, zesty citrus note at the acid end of the white wine spectrum.

cards.name: Gooseberry
cards.blurb: Gooseberry is the tart, faintly musky green berry long used to describe Sauvignon Blanc.

cards.name: Grass
cards.blurb: Grass is the fresh green smell of a just-mown lawn.

cards.name: Peach
cards.blurb: Peach is the juicy stone fruit note of ripe yellow peaches.

cards.name: Petrol
cards.blurb: Petrol is the kerosene-like scent that aged Riesling famously develops.

cards.name: Rose
cards.blurb: Rose is the unmistakable perfume of fresh roses.

cards.name: Tar
cards.blurb: Tar is the dark, resinous scent of warm asphalt.

cards.name: Tomato
cards.blurb: Tomato is the savoury, faintly sweet scent of ripe or stewed tomatoes.

cards.name: Espresso
cards.blurb: Espresso is the dark roasted coffee note in the bass register of a red wine.

cards.name: Strawberry
cards.blurb: Strawberry is the light, sweet note of ripe strawberries.

cards.name: Raspberry
cards.blurb: Raspberry is the perfumed, sweet-tart note of fresh raspberries, sitting between strawberry and cherry in the red fruit spectrum.

cards.name: Fig
cards.blurb: Fig is the dense, honeyed note of fresh ripe figs.

cards.name: Tobacco
cards.blurb: Tobacco is the sweet leafy scent of a cigar box or cured pipe leaf.

cards.name: Dill
cards.blurb: Dill is the distinct pickle-herb scent of dill fronds.

cards.name: Blueberry
cards.blurb: Blueberry is the plush, sweet dark berry note of ripe blueberries.

cards.name: Cocoa
cards.blurb: Cocoa is the dry, dusty cocoa-powder note that coats a red wine's tannin.

cards.name: Bell Pepper
cards.blurb: Bell pepper is the green capsicum scent found in some reds.

cards.name: Graphite
cards.blurb: Graphite is the cool scent of pencil lead, a mineral edge in structured reds.

cards.name: Quince
cards.blurb: Quince is the tart, perfumed orchard fruit note of quince paste, denser than apple or pear.

cards.name: Honey
cards.blurb: Honey is the sweet floral richness of liquid honey.

cards.name: Chamomile
cards.blurb: Chamomile is the gentle, apple-tinged scent of chamomile flowers, a dried flower note rather than a fresh one.

cards.name: Tangerine
cards.blurb: Tangerine is the sweet, fragrant citrus of mandarin peel, softer than orange.

cards.name: Honeysuckle
cards.blurb: Honeysuckle is the heady nectar scent of honeysuckle blossom.

cards.name: Mango
cards.blurb: Mango is the lush tropical note of fully ripe mango flesh.

cards.name: Pomegranate
cards.blurb: Pomegranate is the tangy, lightly bitter red fruit note of pomegranate seeds.

cards.name: Banana
cards.blurb: Banana is the candied banana scent of isoamyl acetate, an ester created by fermentation.

cards.name: Jammy Berry
cards.blurb: Jammy berry is cooked, sugared berry fruit rather than fresh, berries reduced to preserves.

cards.name: Cinnamon
cards.blurb: Cinnamon is the warm bark spice of ground cinnamon.

cards.name: Lemon Curd
cards.blurb: Lemon curd is citrus made rich, lemon folded into butter and sugar.

cards.name: Beeswax
cards.blurb: Beeswax is the soft, waxy polish note of candle wax or honeycomb, sweetness of scent without sugar.

cards.name: Lanolin
cards.blurb: Lanolin is the soft scent of wool grease, clean fleece rather than farmyard.

cards.name: Black Fruit
cards.blurb: Black fruit is a composite of dark berries and plums, fruit read as a mass rather than as any single berry.

cards.name: Game
cards.blurb: Game is the savoury, meaty scent of hung game or cured meat.

cards.name: Sour Cherry
cards.blurb: Sour cherry is the tart note of morello cherries, brighter and sharper than sweet cherry.

cards.name: Licorice
cards.blurb: Licorice is the dark anise-root sweetness of black licorice.

cards.name: Lemon
cards.blurb: Lemon is the fresh citrus note at the heart of most crisp white wines.

cards.name: Mineral
cards.blurb: Mineral is a catch-all for stony, non-fruit freshness, closer to wet rock than to any fruit or flower.

cards.name: Violet
cards.blurb: Violet is the dark floral perfume of violet petals, sweeter and deeper than rose.

cards.name: Lilac
cards.blurb: Lilac is the light spring blossom scent of lilac flowers, airier than violet.

cards.name: Sage
cards.blurb: Sage is the dusty, savoury herb note of dried sage leaves.

cards.name: Green Pepper
cards.blurb: Green pepper is the fresh capsicum bite of an unripe pepper, sharper than the rounded bell pepper note.

cards.name: Lychee
cards.blurb: Lychee is the perfumed, rosewater-tinged tropical note of lychee fruit.

cards.name: Lemon Zest
cards.blurb: Lemon zest is the oily, aromatic side of lemon peel rather than its juice.

cards.name: Orange Blossom
cards.blurb: Orange blossom is the sweet neroli perfume of citrus flowers.

cards.name: Pear
cards.blurb: Pear is the soft orchard fruit note of ripe pears, gentler and rounder than apple.

cards.name: Ginger
cards.blurb: Ginger is the warm, faintly hot spice of fresh ginger root.

cards.name: Apricot
cards.blurb: Apricot is the dense, honeyed stone fruit note of ripe apricots.

cards.name: Sea Salt
cards.blurb: Sea salt is a clean saline impression on the finish, tasted as much as smelled.

cards.name: Grapefruit
cards.blurb: Grapefruit is the bittersweet citrus note of fresh grapefruit flesh and pith.

cards.name: Green Pea
cards.blurb: Green pea is the sweet vegetal scent of freshly podded peas.

cards.name: White Pepper
cards.blurb: White pepper is the sharper, earthier cousin of black pepper spice.

cards.name: Almond
cards.blurb: Almond is the clean bitter-almond note in the finish of many Italian-style whites.

cards.name: Fennel
cards.blurb: Fennel is the fresh anise-and-green scent of fennel bulb and fronds.

cards.name: Herbal Tea
cards.blurb: Herbal tea is the dried infusion scent of tisanes, chamomile, verbena and their kin steeped rather than fresh.

cards.name: Marzipan
cards.blurb: Marzipan is sweet almond paste, richer and more sugared than the plain almond note.

cards.name: Green Apple
cards.blurb: Green apple is the crisp, tart orchard note of an unripe apple, malic acid made fruit.

cards.name: Hazelnut
cards.blurb: Hazelnut is the toasted nut note that white wines earn from lees aging, old oak or gentle oxidation.

cards.name: Saline
cards.blurb: Saline is a briny freshness that makes a wine taste faintly of the sea itself.

cards.name: Leather
cards.blurb: Leather is the scent of worked hide, saddle rather than shoe polish.

cards.name: Black Cherry
cards.blurb: Black cherry is the deep, sweet note of dark cherries, riper and denser than red cherry.

cards.name: Herb
cards.blurb: Herb is a single clean green accent rather than a full herbal bouquet.

cards.name: Black Plum
cards.blurb: Black plum is the dark-skinned plum note, deeper and less sweet than red plum.

cards.name: Green Peppercorn
cards.blurb: Green peppercorn is the fresh, brined bite of unripe peppercorns, greener and juicier than cracked black pepper.

cards.name: Tea Leaf
cards.blurb: Tea leaf is the dry, gently tannic scent of loose black tea.

cards.name: Yuzu Citrus
cards.blurb: Yuzu citrus is the fragrant Japanese citrus note, part grapefruit and part mandarin with a floral edge.

cards.name: Jasmine
cards.blurb: Jasmine is the sweet white-flower perfume of jasmine blossom, headier than orchard bloom.

cards.name: Strawberry Candy
cards.blurb: Strawberry candy is the confected strawberry note of sweet-shop candies rather than fresh fruit.

cards.name: Rose Petal
cards.blurb: Rose petal is a softer, drier take on rose, loose petals rather than full perfume.

cards.name: Smoky Spice
cards.blurb: Smoky spice is spice with an ember behind it, clove and pepper laid over char.

cards.name: White Flower
cards.blurb: White flower is the light blossom scent of small white flowers, acacia and orchard bloom in one impression.

cards.name: Dark Chocolate
cards.blurb: Dark chocolate is the bitter-edged cocoa note, deeper and less sweet than milk chocolate.

cards.name: Dried Herbs
cards.blurb: Dried herbs is the brittle scent of the herb jar, oregano and thyme past their fresh green stage.

cards.name: Red Cherry
cards.blurb: Red cherry is the crisp, mid-weight cherry note between sour cherry and black cherry.

cards.name: Dried Fig
cards.blurb: Dried fig is the concentrated, raisined sweetness of figs dried in the sun.

cards.name: Brioche
cards.blurb: Brioche is the warm scent of buttery yeast bread.

cards.name: Black Pepper
cards.blurb: Black pepper is the direct spice of cracked black peppercorns, warmer and darker than white pepper.

cards.name: Alpine Herbs
cards.blurb: Alpine herbs is the cool scent of mountain meadow plants, gentian and wild thyme in thin air.

cards.name: Chalk
cards.blurb: Chalk is the dry, dusty scent of chalk or limestone dust.

cards.name: Sea Spray
cards.blurb: Sea spray is the fresh iodine-and-salt scent of breaking waves, airier than salt on the palate.

cards.name: Tomato Leaf
cards.blurb: Tomato leaf is the sharp green scent of tomato vines, more herbal and pungent than the fruit itself.

cards.name: Olive
cards.blurb: Olive is the briny, savoury note of black or green olives.

cards.name: Clove
cards.blurb: Clove is the warm, faintly numbing spice of whole cloves.

cards.name: White Peach
cards.blurb: White peach is the delicate cousin of yellow peach, sweeter scented and lower in acid.

cards.name: Sea Breeze
cards.blurb: Sea breeze is a light marine freshness, salt air rather than salt taste.

cards.name: Nutmeg
cards.blurb: Nutmeg is the soft, woody baking spice of freshly grated nutmeg.

cards.name: White Blossom
cards.blurb: White blossom is the airy scent of orchard trees in flower, fainter and fresher than jasmine.

cards.name: Fresh Herbs
cards.blurb: Fresh herbs is the just-cut green scent of living herbs, brighter than the dried jar.

cards.name: Stone
cards.blurb: Stone is the blunt scent of dry rocks in the sun, heavier than chalk and less saline than the sea notes.

cards.name: Pineapple
cards.blurb: Pineapple is the bright tropical note of ripe pineapple flesh.

cards.name: Volcanic Ash
cards.blurb: Volcanic ash is a fine mineral smokiness, ash and warm stone rather than woodsmoke.

cards.name: Blackberry Jam
cards.blurb: Blackberry jam is bramble fruit cooked down to preserves, sweeter and heavier than the fresh berry.
